intro: Atlanta ended San Francisco's unbeaten start and Seattle shut down previously unbeaten Kansas City, so Minnesota is the last undefeated team at 6-0. Lamar Jackson is trending toward a return for Baltimore, and Aaron Rodgers moved past Peyton Manning on the touchdown list in Paris. 160 stories across all 32 teams.

top.label: Biggest Story
top.headline: Falcons knock off the unbeaten 49ers, 29-20
top.dek: Atlanta handed San Francisco its first loss. Michael Penix Jr. threw three touchdown passes and the defense piled up three turnovers. The 49ers head into their bye at 6-1.

top.label: Injury Watch
top.headline: Lamar Jackson trending toward a return for Baltimore
top.dek: Jackson has missed three games with a high ankle sprain. Ian Rapoport reports he is close to 100 percent and expected to play at Buffalo, though the Ravens have not confirmed it. Coach Jesse Minter said the team would know more after Wednesday's practice.

top.label: Player Spotlight
top.headline: Jaxon Smith-Njigba goes for 150 yards in Seattle's rout of Kansas City
top.dek: Smith-Njigba caught 9 passes for 150 yards and a touchdown, with 129 of those yards before halftime. He averages 123.86 receiving yards per game, a pace that would top Calvin Johnson's single-season record of 1,964.

top.label: Stat of the Day
top.headline: 540: Aaron Rodgers' career touchdown passes, third all time
top.dek: Rodgers hit Darnell Washington for a 4-yard score in Paris to pass Peyton Manning. Only Tom Brady and Drew Brees have thrown more. Pittsburgh beat New Orleans 16-10.

top.label: What's Next
top.headline: Browns visit Steelers with first place in the AFC North on the line
top.dek: Cleveland plays at Pittsburgh on Sunday, Nov. 1 at 1 p.m. ET on CBS. Both teams are 5-2. A Browns win would sweep the season series and give them the head-to-head tiebreaker.

teams.name: Buffalo Bills
teams.headline: Bills come off the bye to face Ravens

stories.text: Bills return from the bye with Lamar Jackson on the horizon
stories.summary: Buffalo sits at 5-1 and first in the AFC East after a bye in Week 7. Baltimore is 4-3 and has lost two straight, but Ian Rapoport reports Jackson is nearly recovered from a high ankle sprain and both sides expect him to play. His status depends on how he practices this week.

stories.text: Moore, Oliver and Couch questionable as Gardner-Johnson serves ban
stories.summary: Wide receiver DJ Moore, defensive tackle Ed Oliver and cornerback Te'Cory Couch carry questionable tags into Sunday. Cornerback Jordan Hancock is on injured reserve. Safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson sits out one game without pay after the NFL suspended him for spitting toward Raiders players. The designations come from a preview published before the week's practice reports.

stories.text: Josh Allen leads the league in total touchdowns
stories.summary: Allen has 17 touchdowns through six games, nine passing and eight rushing, tops in the NFL. He is the betting favorite for MVP and says he feels fairly healthy heading into the Ravens game. Buffalo leads the league in points scored.

stories.text: 28.5: points per game the Bills defense allows
stories.summary: The offense scores at will, but the defense gives it back. Buffalo allows 28.5 points per game and ranks next to last against the pass. Sports Illustrated also puts the unit 30th in opponent EPA per play and opponent success rate.

stories.text: Ravens visit Highmark Stadium on Sunday
stories.summary: Buffalo hosts Baltimore on Sunday, Nov. 1, at 1 p.m. ET on CBS. The Bills then travel to Minnesota on Monday, Nov. 9 to face the unbeaten Vikings. Watch whether the secondary holds up if Jackson plays.

teams.name: Miami Dolphins
teams.headline: Dolphins finally win, Hafley gets his first

stories.text: Dolphins beat the Jets 28-25 for their first win of 2026
stories.summary: Miami scored on its first two possessions and held on at MetLife Stadium. Jeff Hafley picked up his first win as Dolphins coach, and the team improved to 1-5. Miami had not led in any game before this one.

stories.text: Achane still out as Douglas returns from injury
stories.summary: Running back De'Von Achane has not played since he was hurt in Week 3, and Ollie Gordon carried the run game again. Rookie receiver Caleb Douglas came back from a three-game absence and scored twice. A Week 8 injury report was not yet available when sources were checked.

stories.text: Malik Willis runs and throws Miami past the Jets
stories.summary: Willis completed 14 of 21 passes for 208 yards and two touchdowns, ran for another score and added 37 rushing yards. He converted two fourth downs with his legs, including the tush push that sealed the win. Next Gen Stats rates his game as the sixth best by a quarterback this season.

stories.text: 23.4%: Chop Robinson's pressure rate leads the NFL
stories.summary: Robinson put five pressures on 23 pass-rush attempts against the Jets. That gives him the league's best pressure rate through seven weeks among players with at least 100 attempts, per Next Gen Stats.

stories.text: Patriots visit Hard Rock Stadium on Sunday
stories.summary: Miami hosts New England on Sunday, Nov. 1, at 4:25 p.m. ET on CBS. The Dolphins' run game has averaged 153.6 yards per game since Week 3, second in the league. The teams meet again in New England in Week 18.

teams.name: New England Patriots
teams.headline: Patriots drop Thursday night game in Chicago

stories.text: Bears beat the Patriots 30-24 on Thursday night
stories.summary: Chicago led 20-14 at the half and held on at Soldier Field. New England fell to 4-3 and sits second in the AFC East behind the 5-1 Bills. The Patriots own the tiebreaker over Buffalo from their Week 4 win.

stories.text: Offensive line shuffles again, Moses plays through foot injury
stories.summary: Third-string guards started at left and right guard against Chicago, and tackle Morgan Moses played on a bad foot. It was the 10th different offensive line combination of the season. A pre-week report lists Ben Brown and Alijah Vera Tucker among those out, but New England's official Week 8 report was not yet confirmed.

stories.text: Drake Maye throws for 321 yards in the loss
stories.summary: Maye went 24 of 31 for 321 yards and accounted for three touchdowns, adding a rushing score. It was his second 300-yard game in three weeks and he has 11 total touchdowns over that stretch. He threw one interception.

stories.text: 10: different offensive line combinations used this season
stories.summary: Injuries keep forcing New England to rework its front. Against Chicago the Patriots managed a 20% success rate on the ground, and the Bears outsnapped them 66-50.

stories.text: Patriots visit the Dolphins on Sunday
stories.summary: New England travels to Hard Rock Stadium on Sunday, Nov. 1, at 4:25 p.m. ET on CBS after a mini-bye. Miami is 1-5 and coming off its first win. The Patriots' turnover margin is minus 7, so watch the ball security.

teams.name: New York Jets
teams.headline: Jets lose to winless Dolphins, Glenn on notice

stories.text: Jets fall to previously winless Dolphins 28-25
stories.summary: New York lost at home to a Miami team that had not won all season. Aaron Glenn defended his late first-half clock management, and he is now 0-8 against AFC East opponents as Jets coach. Pressure on his job is growing.

stories.text: Breece Hall's quad keeps him out since Week 3
stories.summary: Hall has not played since the Lions game in Week 3 and was inactive against Miami, along with guard Dylan Parham. Parham's knee and Hall's quad are the main offensive concerns going into Week 8. No official Week 8 report had been posted when sources were checked.

stories.text: Rookie Omar Cooper Jr. catches five for 115
stories.summary: Cooper caught all five targets for 115 yards and a touchdown against Miami. His 60-yard catch was the Jets' longest play of the season, and he joined Eric Decker as the only Jet this century with two 50-yard catches in a game. He missed four games earlier with an ankle injury.

stories.text: 1: interception by Glenn's defenses in 24 games
stories.summary: The Jets defense has taken the ball away once in 24 games under Glenn. Miami's Malik Willis threw two touchdown passes, matching his total from the entire season before Sunday.

stories.text: Raiders visit MetLife Stadium on Sunday
stories.summary: The Jets host Las Vegas on Sunday, Nov. 1, at 1 p.m. ET on FOX. The Raiders are 3-4 after dropping four straight, with Kirk Cousins starting. New York has lost five of its last six.

teams.name: Baltimore Ravens
teams.headline: Ravens blow a 13-point lead, now 0-2 in division

stories.text: Ravens collapse in the second half against Cincinnati
stories.summary: Baltimore led Cincinnati 13-0 at halftime and lost 35-13 at M&T Bank Stadium. The Ravens outgained the Bengals 258-59 in the first half, then watched Joe Burrow throw four touchdowns after the break. Baltimore is 4-3, 0-2 in the AFC North and last in the division.

stories.text: Lamar Jackson trending toward a return from ankle sprain
stories.summary: Jackson has missed three games with an ankle injury. NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reports he is as close to 100 percent as he has been and is expected to play at Buffalo, though the Ravens have not confirmed it. Jesse Minter said Monday the team would know more after Wednesday's practice.

stories.text: Zay Flowers led the offense in a losing effort
stories.summary: Flowers caught eight passes for 137 yards and a 48-yard touchdown on a screen. Tyler Huntley threw a career-high 298 yards in his third straight start but took four sacks and an interception. Derrick Henry managed 45 yards on 17 carries.

stories.text: 48-0: Opponents' second-half edge over Baltimore in two games
stories.summary: The Ravens have been outscored 48-0 after halftime in their last two games. Against Cincinnati they also committed four false starts and five pre-snap penalties in the first half alone.

stories.text: Ravens visit Josh Allen and the Bills on Sunday
stories.summary: Baltimore plays at Buffalo on Sunday, Nov. 1 at 1 p.m. ET in Orchard Park. The Ravens then host Jacksonville four days later. Watch the quarterback decision and whether the defense can hold a lead for four quarters.

teams.name: Cincinnati Bengals
teams.headline: Bengals erase 13-0 hole, score 35 straight in Baltimore

stories.text: Bengals rally from 13-0 down to beat Baltimore 35-13
stories.summary: Cincinnati trailed at halftime, then scored 35 unanswered points at M&T Bank Stadium and shut out the Ravens in the second half. The win moved the Bengals to 4-2 and was their first AFC North victory of the season.

stories.text: Dugger, Hudson and Bozeman remain on the mend
stories.summary: As of Oct. 19, safety Kyle Dugger was week-to-week with a quad injury, and tight end Tanner Hudson and linebacker Swayze Bozeman were on the Reserve/Injured list. Receiver Colbie Young was close to returning from a knee injury and Andrei Iosivas was on injured reserve. No new injuries were reported from the Baltimore game.

stories.text: Tee Higgins tops 6,000 career receiving yards
stories.summary: Higgins caught six passes for 148 yards and a touchdown in Baltimore and passed 6,000 career receiving yards. Ja'Marr Chase added five catches for 62 yards and a score.

stories.text: 16 of 18: Burrow's second half in Baltimore
stories.summary: Joe Burrow went 16 of 18 for 249 yards and all four of his touchdown passes after halftime. He finished 22 of 30 for 292 yards and has 15 touchdown passes this season.

stories.text: Bengals host 1-6 Titans at Paycor Stadium
stories.summary: Cincinnati hosts Tennessee on Sunday, Nov. 1 at 1 p.m. ET, shown on Local 12 in Cincinnati. The Titans rank 31st in scoring at 15.4 points per game, but Tony Pollard ran for 129 yards and three touchdowns against Cleveland.

teams.name: Cleveland Browns
teams.headline: Browns survive Titans, head to Pittsburgh for first place

stories.text: Browns edge Titans 27-24 on a last-second kick
stories.summary: Tennessee tied it with 58 seconds left, and Andre Szmyt answered with a 32-yard field goal as time expired. Cleveland improved to 5-2 and tied Pittsburgh atop the AFC North. Next Sunday's game at Pittsburgh could decide sole possession of the lead.

stories.text: Dillon Gabriel back from injured reserve
stories.summary: The Browns activated quarterback Dillon Gabriel from injured reserve Monday and waived tight end Carsen Ryan to make room. Deshaun Watson remains the expected starter. Running back Quinshon Judkins returned from an ankle injury against Tennessee and ran for 96 yards.

stories.text: Deshaun Watson posts a season high in Nashville
stories.summary: Watson completed 25 of 36 passes for 308 yards, his best total this season, and ran in a 9-yard go-ahead touchdown in the fourth quarter. Tennessee sacked him only once after he had gone down 24 times in the first six games.

stories.text: 5: Browns wins, all by four points or fewer
stories.summary: Every one of Cleveland's five victories has come by four points or fewer. Szmyt has won three of them with a kick in the final 10 seconds: a 56-yarder against Pittsburgh, a 37-yarder against Baltimore and the 32-yarder against Tennessee.

stories.text: Browns at Steelers with first place on the line
stories.summary: Cleveland visits Pittsburgh on Sunday, Nov. 1 at 1 p.m. ET on CBS at Acrisure Stadium. Both teams are 5-2. The Browns won the first meeting this season, so a win would sweep the series and give them the head-to-head tiebreaker.

teams.name: Pittsburgh Steelers
teams.headline: Steelers grind out a win in Paris, face Browns next

stories.text: Steelers beat Saints 16-10 in the first NFL game in France
stories.summary: Pittsburgh won its third straight at Stade de France and improved to 5-2. The Steelers ran for 150 yards, held New Orleans to 18 on the ground and converted 10 of 16 third downs. Mike McCarthy said the plan was to own the line of scrimmage on both sides.

stories.text: T.J. Watt played through a calf concern in Paris
stories.summary: Watt carried a calf injury into the week, and McCarthy said Oct. 23 he did not expect it to affect his availability. He played against the Saints with two quarterback hits and a near strip-sack. No injuries were reported from the game, and no Week 8 designations have been published yet.

stories.text: Aaron Rodgers climbs to third on the touchdown list
stories.summary: Rodgers threw his 540th career touchdown pass, a 4-yard strike to Darnell Washington, to pass Peyton Manning for third all time. He finished 19 of 30 for 212 yards. Only Tom Brady and Drew Brees have more.

stories.text: 101: Jaylen Warren's rushing yards on 18 carries
stories.summary: Warren ran for 101 yards on 18 carries and added three catches for 36 yards. Linebacker Payton Wilson intercepted Saints quarterback Shough in the red zone, and Patrick Queen led all players with 10 tackles.

stories.text: Steelers host Browns for sole possession of first
stories.summary: Pittsburgh hosts Cleveland on Sunday, Nov. 1 at 1 p.m. ET on CBS. Both teams are 5-2. A Steelers win would put them alone atop the AFC North, while a Browns win would sweep the season series.

teams.name: Houston Texans
teams.headline: Texans hit the bye at 2-5 after OT loss

stories.text: Giants beat Texans in overtime, Houston falls to 2-5
stories.summary: Devin Singletary ran 30 yards for the winning touchdown in overtime, and New York won 27-21 in Houston. Xavier Hutchinson tied it with a 3-yard catch with 52 seconds left, but Houston went three-and-out in the extra period. The Texans are 0-4 at home.

stories.text: Jaylin Noel leaves in a walking boot with a toe injury
stories.summary: Noel hurt his toe in the fourth quarter against the Giants and left the stadium in a boot. DeMeco Ryans called it turf toe, and the report says Noel is likely to miss multiple games. Running back Woody Marks left with a leg issue but returned.

stories.text: Tank Dell returns from his 2024 knee injury
stories.summary: Dell played his first game since the multi-ligament knee injury he suffered in December 2024. He caught one pass for 43 yards against the Giants. Marvin Harrison Jr. also scored his first touchdown as a Texan, a 6-yard catch.

stories.text: 153: C.J. Stroud's passing yards, a season low
stories.summary: Stroud went 17 of 28 for 153 yards and two touchdowns against the Giants. The Houston defense also gave up a season-high 188 rushing yards, with Cam Skattebo running for 124 on 17 carries.

stories.text: Texans are on bye in Week 8, then visit the Chargers
stories.summary: Houston does not play this weekend. The next game is Week 9 at the Los Angeles Chargers. The extra week gives the Texans time to heal Noel's toe and sort out an offense that managed 153 passing yards.

teams.name: Indianapolis Colts
teams.headline: Steichen sticks with Jones after third straight loss

stories.text: Steichen backs Daniel Jones after loss to Vikings
stories.summary: Shane Steichen said the Colts are not considering a quarterback change and have a ton of faith in Jones. Indianapolis lost 16-10 at Minnesota and has dropped three straight. Steichen praised the defense and said the passing game was not where it needed to be.

stories.text: Six Colts are questionable for Jacksonville
stories.summary: Tight end Tyler Warren, receiver Anthony Gould, Bryce Boettcher, cornerback Sauce Gardner, CJ Allen and Justin Walley are all listed as questionable. Alec Pierce is out on injured reserve. Gardner missed the Vikings game with a calf injury.

stories.text: Jonathan Taylor and Seth McGowan carry the Colts offense
stories.summary: Taylor and McGowan ran for 141 yards on 29 carries against Minnesota. Steichen said the plan was to run the ball. Taylor has not yet topped 100 yards in a game this season.

stories.text: 4.9: yards per pass attempt for the Colts against Minnesota
stories.summary: Jones went 13 of 22 for 108 yards, took four sacks and threw an interception on the final possession. Kicker Spencer Shrader also missed from 56 and 48 yards. The Colts scored 10 points.

stories.text: Colts visit first-place Jacksonville on Sunday
stories.summary: Indianapolis plays at the 4-2 Jaguars on Sunday, Nov. 1 at 1 p.m. ET on CBS at EverBank Stadium. Watch whether the Colts can run on a Jacksonville defense that gave up more than 100 rushing yards to Houston.

teams.name: Jacksonville Jaguars
teams.headline: Jaguars lead the South coming off the bye

stories.text: Jaguars sit atop the AFC South after their bye
stories.summary: Jacksonville is 4-2 and leads the division while Indianapolis, Houston and Tennessee all lost in Week 7. The Jaguars play host to the Colts on Sunday and then travel to Baltimore for a Thursday game on Nov. 5.

stories.text: Antonio Johnson and Montaric Brown remain questionable
stories.summary: Safety Antonio Johnson left the loss to Houston with an ankle injury, and cornerback Montaric Brown has a hamstring problem. Liam Coen said both will return to practice but called their availability for Sunday TBD. Tackle Anton Harrison is out on injured reserve.

stories.text: Trevor Lawrence keeps throwing for 300 yards
stories.summary: Lawrence threw for 331 yards against Philadelphia and 306 against Houston, with four touchdown passes in the Houston game. His 14 touchdown passes are tied for fourth in the league.

stories.text: 30th: Jacksonville's rank in passing yards allowed
stories.summary: The Jaguars enter Week 8 with the 30th-ranked pass defense by yards allowed, which is why Johnson and Brown matter. Jacksonville fell 34-31 to Houston on Oct. 18 before the bye.

stories.text: Jaguars host the Colts on Sunday at 1 p.m. ET
stories.summary: Indianapolis visits EverBank Stadium on Nov. 1, with CBS carrying the game. After that Jacksonville plays at Baltimore on Thursday, Nov. 5, then at Tennessee on Nov. 15.

teams.name: Tennessee Titans
teams.headline: Saleh defends Ward after last-play loss

stories.text: Saleh defends Cam Ward after 27-24 loss to Cleveland
stories.summary: Robert Saleh said nobody could watch the film and say Ward did not play good winning football, and pointed at tackling and finishing on defense. Cleveland won on a final-play field goal, and the Titans are 1-6. Ward went 20 of 31 for 181 yards with one interception.

stories.text: Tyjae Spears sits again, and the punter gets hurt
stories.summary: Spears was unavailable against Cleveland, which pushed Tony Pollard into the lead role. The Titans also lost their punter to an injury, so the kicker punted for the first time.

stories.text: Tony Pollard runs for 129 yards and three touchdowns
stories.summary: Pollard carried 25 times for 129 yards and scored three times against the Browns, including a 37-yard run. He leads Tennessee with 478 rushing yards this season.

stories.text: 5.7: Cam Ward's yards per attempt, 32nd of 33 qualifiers
stories.summary: Ward has 1,179 passing yards and has been pressured on 35.5 percent of his dropbacks. Tennessee ranks 32nd in the league in yards per game at 248.6.

stories.text: Titans visit the Bengals on Sunday
stories.summary: Tennessee plays at Cincinnati on Sunday, Nov. 1 at 1 p.m. ET on CBS. Watch Jeffery Simmons, who leads all defensive tackles with 28 quarterback pressures.

teams.name: Denver Broncos
teams.headline: Nix runs wild, Broncos host Chiefs

stories.text: Bo Nix breaks out of his slump with a 62-yard touchdown run
stories.summary: Nix ran for 73 yards and threw for 222 in a 30-16 win at Arizona. His 62-yard scramble before halftime was the longest of his career. Sean Payton backed his quarterback afterward: "He's our guy." Denver has won three straight.

stories.text: Surtain, Hufanga, Allen and Waddle all questionable for Chiefs
stories.summary: Cornerback Patrick Surtain II (ankle) was downgraded to out before kickoff in Arizona. Safety Talanoa Hufanga (ankle), end Zach Allen (hamstring) and receiver Jaylen Waddle (chest) are all listed questionable for Sunday. Denver will watch Thursday and Friday practices before deciding.

stories.text: Jonah Coleman returns and carries the load late
stories.summary: Coleman came back from injury for the first time since Week 2. He ran nine times for 54 yards and caught two passes for 15. J.K. Dobbins added six carries, 23 yards and a touchdown.

stories.text: 13: Broncos plays of 20-plus yards through six games, then five more in one afternoon
stories.summary: Denver had just 13 plays of 20 yards or more in its first six games. Against Arizona it added four more besides Nix's run, including a 52-yard screen to RJ Harvey and a 47-yard catch by Marvin Mims Jr.

stories.text: Chiefs visit Mile High on Sunday
stories.summary: Denver hosts Kansas City on Sunday, Nov. 1 at 4:25 p.m. ET on CBS at Empower Field at Mile High. The Broncos are 5-2 and the Chiefs are 5-1. Watch the cornerback and receiver injury news this week.

teams.name: Kansas City Chiefs
teams.headline: Chiefs look for answers after 20-3 loss

stories.text: Seahawks smother the Chiefs 20-3 on Sunday night
stories.summary: Seattle led from start to finish and held the ball for nearly 36 minutes. Harrison Butker missed a 58-yarder and a 45-yarder. Patrick Mahomes said that if you do not come ready to play, you get your tail kicked in this league.

stories.text: Rashee Rice still battling hamstring as Denver looms
stories.summary: Rice is listed questionable for Sunday after a hamstring injury that has kept him off the practice field for weeks. Tackle Jaylon Moore is also questionable. Tyquan Thornton is on injured reserve with a dislocated ankle. Fox Sports reported Rice sat out the Seattle game.

stories.text: Travis Kelce climbs to fifth on the all-time catch list
stories.summary: Kelce caught four passes for 44 yards on eight targets against Seattle. He now has 1,104 regular-season catches, fifth in NFL history. With Rice out, he remains Mahomes' most reliable target.

stories.text: 0: red zone trips for the Chiefs against Seattle
stories.summary: Kansas City never reached the red zone, the first time that has happened in a Mahomes start. The Chiefs finished with 213 yards, converted 3 of 11 third downs and averaged 4.3 yards per play. Mahomes went 19 of 33 for 165 yards with one interception.

stories.text: At Denver on Sunday for a division showdown
stories.summary: Kansas City visits the Broncos on Sunday, Nov. 1 at 4:25 p.m. ET on CBS. The Chiefs are 5-1 and Denver is 5-2. Watch whether the passing game finds a spark without a healthy Rice.

teams.name: Las Vegas Raiders
teams.headline: Kubiak sticks with Cousins at QB

stories.text: Kubiak says there is no controversy: Cousins starts at the Jets
stories.summary: Coach Klint Kubiak confirmed Kirk Cousins as the Week 8 starter. Rookie Fernando Mendoza, the No. 1 pick, will play at some point but not this week. The Raiders have lost four straight after a 3-0 start.

stories.text: Patrick Johnson questionable as Raiders head to New York
stories.summary: Patrick Johnson is listed questionable for Sunday. Carter Runyon and Dont'e Thornton are on injured reserve. The Jets list five players as questionable, including running back Breece Hall.

stories.text: Cousins throws for 295 yards in a lost cause
stories.summary: Cousins completed 26 of 44 passes for 295 yards and two touchdowns against the Rams. He hit Tre Tucker for 37 yards and Ashton Jeanty for 15 in the fourth quarter. Two failed conversions kept Las Vegas from closing the gap.

stories.text: 31st: where the Raiders rank in rushing yards per game
stories.summary: The passing game sits in the top 10, but the run game, led by Jeanty, ranks 31st in yards per game. The defense is 29th in both points and yards allowed. Cousins leads the league with 16 touchdown passes.

stories.text: At the Jets on Sunday afternoon
stories.summary: Las Vegas visits the Jets on Sunday, Nov. 1 at 1 p.m. ET on FOX at MetLife Stadium. The Raiders are 3-4 and the Jets are 2-5. Watch whether the run game can wake up against the Jets.

teams.name: Los Angeles Chargers
teams.headline: Winless Chargers come off the bye

stories.text: Harbaugh will not rule out changes at 0-6
stories.summary: Jim Harbaugh said the winless Chargers are looking at everything during the bye week. He said 0-6 does not give a team the privilege of ruling anything out. The staff is weighing a simpler playbook to help the offense.

stories.text: Alt, James and Harris targeted for a Week 8 return
stories.summary: Harbaugh hopes to get tackle Joe Alt (neck), safety Derwin James (hamstring) and receiver Tre' Harris (hamstring) back for the Rams. Injuries on the offensive line have forced four rookies into action at times. Confirm their status when the practice report comes out.

stories.text: Justin Herbert is taking a beating behind a patched line
stories.summary: Herbert is completing 59.4% of his passes, well below his 66.1% career mark. He has five touchdowns and 10 turnovers, including eight interceptions. Harbaugh pointed to too many desperation plays this season.

stories.text: 99: dropbacks under pressure for Herbert, most in the league
stories.summary: No quarterback has faced pressure on more dropbacks than Herbert's 99. He has also been sacked 21 times, second most in the league, nine of them in the last two games.

stories.text: At the Rams on Sunday afternoon
stories.summary: Los Angeles visits the Rams at SoFi Stadium on Sunday, Nov. 1, kickoff 1:05 p.m. PT (4:05 p.m. ET) on FOX. Houston follows on Nov. 8. Watch the offensive line and whether Harbaugh's bye-week tweaks show up.

teams.name: Dallas Cowboys
teams.headline: Run game wakes up, Dallas passes Philly

stories.text: Cowboys run past Eagles 38-21 and climb the NFC East ladder
stories.summary: Dallas ended a two-game losing streak on Monday night in Philadelphia. The lead changed hands six times before CeeDee Lamb's 16-yard touchdown and a two-point conversion put the Cowboys up 28-21 late in the third quarter. The win moves Dallas to 3-4 and ahead of the 2-5 Eagles.

stories.text: Left tackle Tyler Guyton hurts his back against Philadelphia
stories.summary: Guyton hurt his back on the offense's last drive Monday night. The first x-rays looked good, but the team planned more tests. Dallas protected Dak Prescott well enough that he went down zero times, so a long absence would sting up front.

stories.text: Javonte Williams posts a career-high 155 rushing yards
stories.summary: Williams carried 25 times for 155 yards and a touchdown against the Eagles. He is the first Cowboys back to run for 150 yards in a game since Ezekiel Elliott in 2018. Dallas came in ranked 31st in rushing offense.

stories.text: 204: rushing yards for a Cowboys team that averaged 76
stories.summary: Dallas entered Monday ranked 31st in the league at 76 rushing yards per game and had the fewest carries in the NFL. Against Philadelphia the Cowboys ran 38 times for 204 yards. It was the second-most rushing yards the Eagles have allowed in Vic Fangio's three seasons as defensive coordinator.

stories.text: Arizona visits AT&T Stadium on Sunday at 1 p.m. ET
stories.summary: The Cowboys host the Cardinals on Sunday, Nov. 1 at 1 p.m. ET on FOX. It is a short week after Monday night. Watch whether Dallas keeps feeding Williams and the offensive line after the Guyton scare.

teams.name: New York Giants
teams.headline: Giants hit the bye alone atop the East

stories.text: Giants beat Houston in overtime and take the bye with the division lead
stories.summary: Devin Singletary broke a 30-yard run with 7:25 left in overtime to give the Giants a 27-21 win at Houston. New York is 4-2-1 and leads the NFC East going into Week 8. J.J. McCarthy made his first start as the team's third quarterback this season.

stories.text: Tyrone Tracy Jr. heads to injured reserve with a hamstring
stories.summary: Tracy hurt his hamstring in the win at Houston and goes on injured reserve, which means at least four missed games. GM Joe Schoen said the injury is not expected to be long term. The Giants signed Gregory Desrosiers from the Chargers' practice squad and lean on Devin Singletary and Cam Skattebo.

stories.text: Malik Nabers strings together four straight 100-yard games
stories.summary: Nabers became the second player in Giants history with four consecutive 100-yard receiving games. He opened the Houston game with a 42-yard catch from McCarthy, who went 5-for-5 for 96 yards to start. McCarthy finished 20 of 28 for 252 yards.

stories.text: 4: rushing touchdowns, a first for the Giants since 1950
stories.summary: New York ran for four touchdowns in the win at Houston, the first time the franchise has done that since 1950. Cam Skattebo rushed for a career-high 124 yards, and the Giants held Houston to 84 rushing yards.

stories.text: Bye week, then a trip to Philadelphia on Nov. 8
stories.summary: The Giants are off in Week 8. They play at the Eagles on Sunday, Nov. 8 at 1 p.m. ET on FOX, then host Washington on Thursday night. GM Joe Schoen said the trade deadline is Nov. 10 and that he will review the roster with coach John Harbaugh.

teams.name: Philadelphia Eagles
teams.headline: Eagles drop a fifth straight at home

stories.text: Eagles lose a fifth straight, their longest skid since 2016
stories.summary: Philadelphia led 21-20 after a 17-play, 84-yard drive to open the third quarter, then Dallas scored 18 unanswered points in a 38-21 win. The Eagles are 2-5 with Jalen Hurts out and Tanner McKee at quarterback. Dallas finished with 416 yards.

stories.text: Barkley, Pierce and Covey all hurt in the Dallas loss
stories.summary: Saquon Barkley tweaked his hamstring early and left with a back injury, though he told reporters he did not expect either to keep him out next week. Dameon Pierce left in the fourth quarter with an undisclosed injury, and Britain Covey went out with a knee. DeVonta Smith (hamstring), Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) and Nolan Smith (concussion) were inactive.

stories.text: Rookie Makai Lemon leads the Eagles with seven catches
stories.summary: Lemon caught seven passes for 67 yards and scored his first career touchdown against Dallas. Tanner McKee threw to him all night, going 23 of 35 for 211 yards with one touchdown and a late interception.

stories.text: 8: sacks through seven games, fewest in the NFL
stories.summary: The Eagles put $328 million into Jalen Carter, Jonathan Greenard and Jordan Davis, and the line got no sacks, quarterback hits or tackles for loss against Dallas. Eight sacks through seven games is the league low among teams that have played seven. The last Eagles team that low at this point played in 1993.

stories.text: Eagles visit Washington on Sunday Night Football
stories.summary: Philadelphia plays at the Commanders on Sunday, Nov. 1 at 8:20 p.m. ET on NBC. The league kept the game in prime time because both teams could have been playing for first place in the NFC East. Barkley's back and the health of the backfield are the first things to watch this week.

teams.name: Washington Commanders
teams.headline: Commanders return from the bye without McLaurin

stories.text: Commanders enter the post-bye stretch at a crossroads
stories.summary: Washington is 1-4-1 and two games back in the NFC East. Terry McLaurin is out for the year with a torn left patellar tendon, and the Eagles and Rams come next, both before the trade deadline. Dan Quinn added veteran defensive coach Steve Wilks as an adviser during the break.

stories.text: Mariota and Omenihu work back into practice
stories.summary: Quarterback Marcus Mariota (knee) and edge Charles Omenihu (groin) will return to practice after missing two games since the Oct. 4 loss to Indianapolis. Javon Kinlaw is recovering more slowly than the team hoped. Edge Javontae Jean-Baptiste is on injured reserve.

stories.text: Jayden Daniels throws for 300 yards in the last game
stories.summary: Daniels completed 29 of 40 passes for 300 yards and two touchdowns in the 23-17 loss at San Francisco before the bye. He is available for Sunday. Quinn said Antonio Williams is the likely next receiver to see more targets with McLaurin gone.

stories.text: 81.82%: opponent touchdown rate in the red zone
stories.summary: Washington lets opponents score touchdowns on 81.82 percent of red zone trips and allows 28.7 points per game. The offense scores 22.0 points per game and wins the turnover battle at plus 1.0 per game. The red zone defense is the main concern against Philadelphia.

stories.text: Eagles come to Landover on Sunday night
stories.summary: The Commanders host Philadelphia on Sunday, Nov. 1 at 8:20 p.m. ET on NBC. The Eagles won the first meeting 24-22 on Sept. 13. Washington comes off a bye against a team on a five-game losing streak.

teams.name: Chicago Bears
teams.headline: Bears beat Patriots, face Seattle on Monday

stories.text: Bears hold off Patriots 30-24 on Thursday night
stories.summary: Chicago beat New England at Soldier Field to reach 5-2 and stay second in the NFC North. The Bears played the Patriots on a short week and sat idle on Sunday while Minnesota stayed unbeaten. The Vikings still lead the division by more than a game.

stories.text: Cole Kmet done for the season with a knee injury
stories.summary: The Bears put their tight end on injured reserve Friday after he could not bear weight on his right leg. Kmet got hurt on an 8-yard catch with 5:46 left against New England. He had 10 catches for 87 yards this year. Ben Johnson said the offense will not change, and Colston Loveland and rookie Sam Roush take on bigger roles.

stories.text: Luther Burden III turns short catches into big gains
stories.summary: Burden caught four passes for 130 yards and a touchdown against the Patriots. One was a 58-yard gain that got the offense moving early. Caleb Williams threw for 308 yards and two scores with a 116.7 passer rating.

stories.text: 163: Williams' yards after the catch on 308 passing yards
stories.summary: More than half of Caleb Williams' passing yards against New England came after the catch. Burden gained 91 of those himself. On defense, the Bears held the Patriots to 2 of 7 on third down.

stories.text: Bears visit Seahawks on Monday Night Football
stories.summary: Chicago plays at Seattle on Monday, Nov. 2 at 8:15 p.m. ET on ESPN. The Seahawks are 4-3 after beating Kansas City 20-3, but left tackle Charles Cross left that game with an ankle injury. The Bears do not release an injury report until Thursday because of the Monday game.

teams.name: Detroit Lions
teams.headline: Lions host unbeaten Vikings on Sunday

stories.text: Jake Bates wins it at the gun, Lions beat Packers 20-17
stories.summary: Bates hit a 22-yard field goal as time expired at Ford Field. Detroit drove 71 yards in 10 plays and ran out the final 3:21 to set up the kick. The Lions now have back-to-back wins for the first time since early October of last season.

stories.text: St. Brown and Rakestraw nurse minor ankle injuries
stories.summary: Amon-Ra St. Brown tweaked his ankle and cornerback Ennis Rakestraw Jr. left the Packers game with one. Both are expected to rest Wednesday and try to practice Thursday. Dan Campbell does not view Rakestraw's injury as serious, and neither player's status for Sunday is expected to change.

stories.text: Brian Branch returns from Achilles tear with an interception
stories.summary: Branch played his first game of the season against Green Bay and intercepted a pass in the fourth quarter. He came back from a torn Achilles. Detroit held the Packers to 17 points, the fewest the Lions have allowed this season.

stories.text: 6: straight games with a Goff touchdown and no interception
stories.summary: Jared Goff opened the season with at least one touchdown pass and no picks in each of Detroit's first six games. Only Russell Wilson, Alex Smith and Milt Plum had done that before him. Goff went 22 of 32 for 303 yards and two scores against the Packers.

stories.text: Lions host 6-0 Vikings at Ford Field
stories.summary: Detroit hosts Minnesota on Sunday, Nov. 1 at 1:00 p.m. ET on FOX. Campbell wants a better run game, and center Cade Mays returned against Green Bay to help with that. The Lions gained 119 rushing yards on a 3.6 average last week.

teams.name: Green Bay Packers
teams.headline: Packers bounce back vs Panthers on Thursday?

stories.text: Two missed kicks cost Packers in 20-17 loss to Detroit
stories.summary: Trey Smack missed a field goal on the opening drive and had a 35-yarder blocked late. Green Bay scored on one of four red zone trips and failed on a fourth-and-four at the Detroit seven. The loss drops the Packers to 4-3 and last place in the division.

stories.text: Matthew Golden misses second straight practice
stories.summary: The receiver sat out Tuesday with shoulder and foot injuries. He first hurt the shoulder against Detroit and finished that game. Golden leads Green Bay with 69 targets, 36 catches and 540 yards, so his status for Thursday matters.

stories.text: Christian Watson sits second in the league in receiving TDs
stories.summary: Watson has six receiving touchdowns, second in the NFL, and ranks sixth in receiving yards. He has 15 explosive plays. Green Bay leans on him and Golden while the run game struggles.

stories.text: 59.9: rushing yards per game, last in the NFL
stories.summary: The Packers rank 32nd in rushing. Josh Jacobs returned against Detroit with 11 carries for 36 yards, and he added five catches for 55 yards and a touchdown. Jordan Love leads the passing attack at 279.7 yards per game, fourth in the league.

stories.text: Panthers visit Lambeau on Thursday night
stories.summary: Green Bay hosts Carolina on Thursday, Oct. 29 at 8:15 p.m. ET on Prime Video. Watch Golden's status and whether the Packers can fix the kicking game and the red zone after the Detroit loss.

teams.name: Minnesota Vikings
teams.headline: Unbeaten Vikings head to Detroit

stories.text: Vikings grind out 16-10 win over Colts to stay unbeaten
stories.summary: Minnesota is the only unbeaten team left in the NFC. The offense gained 275 yards, and the defense allowed 215, sacked Daniel Jones four times and took the ball away once. The Vikings lead the NFC North with Chicago 5-2 behind them.

stories.text: Aaron Jones day-to-day, Caleb Banks left with lower-body injury
stories.summary: Jones aggravated his sprained left knee late against Indianapolis, and Kevin O'Connell called him day-to-day. Defensive tackle Caleb Banks left the game with a lower-body injury and did not return. Receivers Jordan Addison and Myles Price cleared concussion checks during the game.

stories.text: Jordan Mason back from thumb fracture, leads the ground game
stories.summary: Mason returned from a fractured thumb and carried 15 times for 68 yards against the Colts, the most on the team. Jones managed 26 yards on eight carries before taking the hit to his knee. O'Connell said he does not see Jones' status as a depth problem.

stories.text: 12.3: points per game allowed, fewest in the NFL
stories.summary: Minnesota allows nearly five fewer points per game than second-ranked Kansas City and leads the league in third-down defense. The Vikings have not given up a fourth-quarter touchdown during their 11-game winning streak. Blake Cashman leads the team with 54 tackles and 4.5 sacks.

stories.text: Vikings put 6-0 on the line at Detroit
stories.summary: Minnesota visits the 4-2 Lions on Sunday, Nov. 1 at 1:00 p.m. ET on FOX. Detroit's offense has Jared Goff at 14 touchdowns with no interceptions, so the Vikings' defense faces its toughest test yet.

teams.name: Atlanta Falcons
teams.headline: Falcons stop the unbeaten 49ers, 29-20

stories.text: Falcons knock off previously unbeaten 49ers 29-20
stories.summary: Atlanta snapped a two-game skid and handed San Francisco its first loss. Michael Penix Jr. threw three touchdown passes and the defense piled up three turnovers and three forced fumbles. It was also the Falcons' first win at Mercedes-Benz Stadium this season.

stories.text: A.J. Terrell returns while tackle Michael Jerrell lands on IR
stories.summary: Cornerback A.J. Terrell Jr. came off injured reserve before the 49ers game and sits atop the Week 8 depth chart, with C.J. Henderson behind him. Tackle Michael Jerrell went on injured reserve with a biceps injury, so rookie Ethan Onianwa is now the backup right tackle behind Jawaan Taylor. The team had not posted a Week 8 injury report when the depth chart came out.

stories.text: Kendal Daniels answers a scary week with two takeaways
stories.summary: Daniels left the field on a stretcher the week before with a neck injury and went to Grady Memorial Hospital. He cleared in time to play the 49ers, wore the green dot in place of the injured Divine Deablo, and led Atlanta with 11 tackles. He also intercepted Brock Purdy and recovered a fumble late, and the team gave him a game ball.

stories.text: 907: Bijan Robinson's scrimmage yards through seven games
stories.summary: Robinson put up 122 yards from scrimmage against the 49ers and has 907 for the season. Atlanta has scored 31.0 points per game over its last five weeks, per Tampa Bay's own game preview.

stories.text: Falcons visit Buccaneers Sunday at 1 p.m. ET on FOX
stories.summary: Atlanta plays at Raymond James Stadium in a division game. Tampa Bay held the league's previous leading passer to 163 yards and has 10 sacks over its last two games, so Penix's protection is the thing to watch. Kyle Pitts has given the Bucs trouble before. Atlanta leads the all-time series 33-32.

teams.name: Carolina Panthers
teams.headline: Panthers regroup for Thursday night at Lambeau

stories.text: Four turnovers sink Panthers in 43-13 loss to Tampa Bay
stories.summary: Carolina fell behind 17-0 early and trailed 33-6 at halftime. Bryce Young threw two interceptions and lost a fumble on a strip-sack that Calijah Kancey returned 32 yards for a score. The four turnovers led to 20 Tampa Bay points, and the Panthers dropped to 3-3.

stories.text: Four Panthers sit out Tuesday walk-through ahead of Packers
stories.summary: Outside linebacker Jaelan Phillips (hamstring), guard Damien Lewis (knee), guard Torricelli Simpkins (ankle) and cornerback Akayleb Evans (triceps and knee) did not take part. Bryce Young (knee), Jalen Coker (shoulder) and Bobby Brown III (hand) were full participants. Right tackle Taylor Moton went on injured reserve after re-injuring himself against Tampa Bay, and cornerbacks Jaycee Horn and Mike Jackson remain on IR.

stories.text: Bryce Young keeps pace with Cam Newton's 2011 yardage
stories.summary: Young went 14 of 27 for 163 yards and a touchdown against Tampa Bay. He has 1,712 passing yards through six games, second only to Newton's 1,847 in 2011 for a Panthers quarterback. He has thrown a touchdown pass in eight straight games, playoffs included.

stories.text: 258: rushing yards the Panthers allowed on 49 carries
stories.summary: The 49 carries matched the franchise record for rushing attempts allowed. Carolina's run defense was already giving up 153.2 yards per game, the most in the league, going into Thursday's game at Green Bay.

stories.text: Panthers at Packers Thursday, 8:15 p.m. ET on Prime Video
stories.summary: Carolina plays at Lambeau Field on a short week. Green Bay has the league's worst rushing offense at 59.9 yards per game, which sets up a test for the league's most generous run defense. Pass protection also matters: Young has been sacked at a 6.94 percent rate with several linemen out.

teams.name: New Orleans Saints
teams.headline: Saints use the bye to evaluate everything

stories.text: Moore opens a self-scout week at 2-5
stories.summary: After a 16-10 loss to Pittsburgh in Paris, coach Kellen Moore said the bye week will include a review of the kicker decision and the coaching staff, coordinators Doug Nussmeier and Brandon Staley included. Finding points, starting with the run game, is his first priority. The Saints have not made the playoffs since the 2020 season.

stories.text: Justin Reid and CJ Donaldson hurt in Paris
stories.summary: Safety Justin Reid left the Steelers game with a concussion and running back CJ Donaldson with a shoulder injury. New Orleans is off in Week 8, which gives both extra time before the Nov. 8 game against Cleveland. No updated designations have been posted.

stories.text: Tyler Shough throws 38 times and keeps the offense moving
stories.summary: Shough completed 30 of 38 passes for 278 yards with a touchdown and a red-zone interception in Paris. He has 13 touchdown passes and six interceptions on the year. He also led the Saints in rushing with 7 yards.

stories.text: 18: rushing yards on 17 carries, the Saints' fewest in 27 years
stories.summary: Kendre Miller had 6 yards on 8 carries and Alvin Kamara 5 on 6. New Orleans ranks 26th in rushing at 86 yards per game, and its defense ranks 29th against the run.

stories.text: Saints are on bye, then host Browns Nov. 8
stories.summary: New Orleans has no game in Week 8. Its next one is against Cleveland on Nov. 8 at the Caesars Superdome. Kicker Daniel Carlson, who missed a 52-yarder in Paris, is one issue under review.

teams.name: Tampa Bay Buccaneers
teams.headline: Bucs get first division win, host Atlanta

stories.text: Bucs rout Panthers 43-13 for first division win
stories.summary: Tampa Bay led 33-6 at halftime and forced four Carolina turnovers. Baker Mayfield came back from a thumb injury that cost him three games. The Bucs moved to 2-5 and host Atlanta on Sunday.

stories.text: Egbuka, Goedeke and Winfield all questionable for Falcons
stories.summary: Receiver Emeka Egbuka (concussion and foot) missed the Carolina game and has not cleared yet. Coach Todd Bowles said the team will evaluate him Wednesday and Thursday. Guard Luke Goedeke and safety Antoine Winfield Jr. are also questionable.

stories.text: Calijah Kancey scores off a strip-sack
stories.summary: Al-Quadin Muhammad stripped Bryce Young, and Kancey scooped the ball and ran 32 yards for a touchdown. Zyon McCollum also picked off a Young pass. Tampa Bay's defense has 10 sacks over its last two games.

stories.text: 258: rushing yards for the Bucs against Carolina
stories.summary: Tampa Bay ground out 258 yards on the ground in the win. Atlanta also wants to run the ball Sunday, so the game could come down to who wins the line of scrimmage.

stories.text: Falcons visit Raymond James Sunday at 1 p.m. ET on FOX
stories.summary: Tampa Bay hosts Atlanta in Week 8 on Sunday, Nov. 1. The Falcons just beat the 49ers behind three Michael Penix Jr. touchdown passes. Atlanta leads the all-time series 33-32.

teams.name: Arizona Cardinals
teams.headline: Fitzgerald night ends in another home loss

stories.text: Broncos spoil Fitzgerald's night as Arizona drops to 2-5
stories.summary: Denver beat Arizona 30-16 at State Farm Stadium on the day the Cardinals retired Larry Fitzgerald's No. 11 and put him in the Ring of Honor. Bo Nix broke a 6-6 tie with a long touchdown run, and RJ Harvey added a 52-yard score on a screen. Coach Mike LaFleur said he was frustrated with the way his team played.

stories.text: Jeremiyah Love set to practice Wednesday after ankle absence
stories.summary: The rookie running back has missed two straight games with a new ankle injury, separate from the one he had in the preseason. The team said injured reserve was never on the table. LaFleur said Love will be at Wednesday's practice, and that session will set the tone for his status against Dallas.

stories.text: Trey McBride keeps producing on a losing team
stories.summary: McBride caught 10 passes on 13 targets for 111 yards and a touchdown against Denver. It was his ninth career game with 100 or more receiving yards. His third-quarter score was Arizona's only red zone touchdown across its last two games.

stories.text: 10: Arizona's franchise-record home losing streak
stories.summary: The loss to Denver stretched the Cardinals' home losing streak to 10 games, a franchise record. Arizona has not won at State Farm Stadium in that span, and the next home game is Nov. 15 against the Rams.

stories.text: Cardinals visit Dallas on Sunday
stories.summary: Arizona plays at Dallas on Sunday, Nov. 1 at 1:00 p.m. ET on FOX. The Cowboys rank 30th in total defense and 31st in run defense at 149.8 yards allowed per game. Watch whether Love is healthy enough to test that front.

teams.name: Los Angeles Rams
teams.headline: Rams end skid, wait on Garrett's knee

stories.text: Rams beat Raiders 35-21 to snap a two-game skid
stories.summary: Los Angeles ran past Las Vegas on the road and moved to 3-4. Matthew Stafford threw three touchdowns, and the Rams got 192 rushing yards from two backs. The Raiders kept it close through the air, with Kirk Cousins throwing for 295 yards.

stories.text: Myles Garrett still not practicing, McVay noncommittal
stories.summary: Garrett is just over six weeks removed from knee surgery and has missed six games after going on injured reserve following Week 1. Sean McVay said he has not decided on his return. NFL Media reported Garrett could practice this week and play against the Chargers, but if he is not practicing by Thursday, he is unlikely to play.

stories.text: Stafford efficient in Las Vegas
stories.summary: Stafford completed 23 of 29 passes for 195 yards, three touchdowns and one interception. Puka Nacua caught 8 passes for 68 yards and a score on 10 targets, and tight end Davis Allen caught two touchdowns.

stories.text: 192: rushing yards from Kyren Williams and Blake Corum
stories.summary: Williams ran 16 times for 99 yards and a touchdown. Corum added 17 carries for 93 yards and a touchdown. The Rams' front also held the Raiders to 48 rushing yards.

stories.text: Chargers visit SoFi on Sunday afternoon
stories.summary: The Rams host the Chargers on Sunday, Nov. 1 at 4:05 p.m. ET on FOX. Los Angeles has the league's last-ranked scoring offense and the worst EPA per play, with four rookies among its five offensive line starters. Watch the Rams' pass rush against that line.

teams.name: San Francisco 49ers
teams.headline: Niners fall to Falcons, head into bye

stories.text: Turnovers sink 49ers in 29-20 loss to Falcons
stories.summary: San Francisco lost its first game of the season in Atlanta and enters the bye at 6-1. The 49ers gave the ball away four times and forced none, per the team's review. Brock Purdy threw two interceptions and took a sack on fourth down.

stories.text: McCaffrey has a mild hamstring strain
stories.summary: Kyle Shanahan said the injury is a mild hamstring strain, not the thigh problem first feared. Shanahan said he and McCaffrey are both optimistic about his availability after the bye. Nick Bosa, Mike Evans and Deebo Samuel could also return after the bye, though none is guaranteed.

stories.text: Kittle produces despite late fumble
stories.summary: George Kittle caught 8 passes for 88 yards against heavy coverage, but he fumbled on the final drive. Fred Warner led the defense with 13 tackles, and Dre Greenlaw had 12.

stories.text: 42: pass calls to 21 runs against Atlanta
stories.summary: Shanahan called twice as many passes as runs even though the offense averaged 5.3 yards per carry. Purdy took the brunt of the turnover trouble through the air.

stories.text: Bye in Week 8, then the Raiders
stories.summary: San Francisco is off in Week 8. The Week 9 game against the Raiders was moved to a 4:25 p.m. ET kickoff on FOX. Injured starters get another week to heal before it.

teams.name: Seattle Seahawks
teams.headline: Seahawks smother Chiefs, then Cross hurts ankle

stories.text: Seahawks hand Chiefs their first loss, 20-3
stories.summary: Seattle ended a two-game skid by shutting down Kansas City on Sunday night and moved to 4-3. The Chiefs finished with 213 total yards, no touchdowns and never reached the red zone. Patrick Mahomes threw for 165 yards and an interception.

stories.text: Charles Cross ankle injury leaves Bears game in doubt
stories.summary: Cross left the Chiefs game in the fourth quarter. Ian Rapoport reported a high ankle sprain with a one to two week recovery, but Mike Macdonald called it only an ankle injury and is taking it day by day. Josh Jones replaced Cross at left tackle. Rashid Shaheed (knee) and Velus Jones Jr. (hamstring) also got hurt.

stories.text: Jaxon Smith-Njigba goes for 150 yards
stories.summary: Smith-Njigba caught 9 passes for 150 yards and a touchdown, with 129 of those yards coming before halftime. He averages 123.86 receiving yards per game, a pace that would break Calvin Johnson's single-season record of 1,964 yards.

stories.text: 36: Kenneth Walker III's rushing yards on 14 carries
stories.summary: Seattle's defense held its former back well below his 133.0 rushing yards per game average. The performance ended Walker's streak of 11 straight games with at least 50 rushing yards. Kansas City went 3 of 11 on third down.

stories.text: Bears come to Seattle on Monday night
stories.summary: Seattle hosts Chicago on Monday, Nov. 2 at 8:15 p.m. ET on ESPN. Running backs Zach Charbonnet and Jadarian Price will practice this week, and Charbonnet has a chance to make his 2026 debut. Cross's status is the main question.
